Convert to Markdown

sbf_as_md.Rd

Converts a data frame to the lines of a markdown table in the same format as the .md file saved by sbf_save_table() and sbf_save_plot().

Usage

sbf_as_md(
  x,
  round = FALSE,
  proportion = FALSE,
  format_column = list(),
  round_as_estimate = character(0),
  no_big_mark = character(0)
)

Arguments

x

A data frame.

round

A flag specifying whether to round the numeric columns as in the .md file saved by sbf_save_table() (described there), in which case significant trailing zeros are kept. If FALSE the values are not rounded.

proportion

A flag specifying whether the columns estimate, lower, upper and sd are proportions, in which case significant digits are counted from the nearer of 0 and 1 in the .md file.

format_column

A list of two-sided formulas of the form column ~ fun(.) specifying how to round and format numeric columns other than estimate, lower, upper and sd in the .md file. The function can return a numeric vector, which is formatted without further rounding, or a character vector, which is used as is. The values in the .rds and .csv files are not altered.

round_as_estimate

A character vector of numeric columns, other than estimate, lower, upper, sd and svalue, to round in the .md file to the same number of decimal places as estimate in the same row (e.g. an observed value compared with the estimate). Rows with a missing estimate are formatted as data. If proportion = TRUE the columns must also be proportions.

no_big_mark

A character vector of numeric columns (e.g. year) to format without commas as thousands separators in the .md file.

Value

A character vector of the lines of the table in markdown format.

Details

Numeric columns are right-aligned with their decimal points aligned using spaces and commas as thousands separators for numbers of 1000 or more except in the columns named by no_big_mark. Other columns, including numbers stored as character, are left-aligned. List columns and the geometry column of sf objects are dropped.

See also

sbf_round_data()

Examples

x <- data.frame(
  term = c("bIntercept", "bYear"),
  estimate = c(0.53124, 12.3456),
  lower = c(0.21234, 9.8765),
  upper = c(0.87012, 15.4321)
)
writeLines(sbf_as_md(x))
#> | term       | estimate |   lower |    upper |
#> | :--------- | -------: | ------: | -------: |
#> | bIntercept |  0.53124 | 0.21234 |  0.87012 |
#> | bYear      | 12.3456  | 9.8765  | 15.4321  |
writeLines(sbf_as_md(x, round = TRUE))
#> | term       | estimate | lower | upper |
#> | :--------- | -------: | ----: | ----: |
#> | bIntercept |     0.53 |  0.21 |  0.87 |
#> | bYear      |    12.3  |  9.9  | 15    |
writeLines(sbf_as_md(data.frame(year = 2025L, count = 1500L)))
#> |  year | count |
#> | ----: | ----: |
#> | 2,025 | 1,500 |
writeLines(sbf_as_md(data.frame(year = 2025L), no_big_mark = "year"))
#> | year |
#> | ---: |
#> | 2025 |
